generated_by: generate_tables.py, generate_tickets.py, generate_corpus_pdfs.py, hand-written policies/ and eval/ (see `sources`)
reference_clock_note: All dates are anchored here, never the wall clock, so runs are reproducible.

pdf.note: Lossy on purpose: heading markers dropped, tables flattened, running header + page number on every page. Produced by generate_corpus_pdfs.py; ingested by rag.ingest.load_policy_corpus_pdf.

A_policy_corpus.composition: 5 core (returns, refunds, shipping, escalation SOP, FAQ) + 5 category addenda + refund authorisation matrix, warranty, fraud prevention, cancellation
deliberate_conflicts: Return window: general 30 days (RP-1.1) vs electronics 15 (CA-EL-1.1), apparel 45 (CA-AP-1.1), groceries non-returnable (CA-GR-1.1), home 30 (CA-HM-1.1), beauty 10 (CA-BT-1.1). RP-1.4 states that the category addendum wins.
Festive window: general 45 days (RP-1.2) vs electronics 30 (CA-EL-1.2), apparel 60 (CA-AP-1.2), beauty none (CA-BT-1.2).
Defective-item report window: 60 days (RP-1.3) vs groceries 48 hours (CA-GR-1.2) and breakables 7 days (CA-HM-2.1).
near_duplicates: Opened-seal rules appear in RP-3.2, CA-EL-2.1, CA-BT-2.1, CA-AP-2.2 with different scope.
Approval tiers appear in RF-3, ESC-1 and RA-1 and must agree.
A_policy_corpus.provenance: Generated for this capstone; no third-party text. No retailer publishes a redistributable returns policy.

B_intake_tickets.ground_truth: intent, category, order_id (the reference VISIBLE in the text, else null), customer_id, sentiment, urgency, requires_human_review, contains_injection_attempt; extension adds scenario, expected_route, expected_escalation_codes, expected_behavior.
B_intake_tickets.taxonomy_source: Intent names follow Bitext's retail/e-commerce taxonomy (CDLA-Sharing 1.0). No Bitext text is included - all ticket text is generated.

layers.base: 60 customers / 120 orders / 15 refunds (byte-stable; tests and docs cite it)
layers.extension: +90 customers / +480 orders; own RNG; append-only; abuse flags meet the written FP-1 definition

C_mock_api_tables.note: Equivalent five-table set (customers, products, orders, shipments, refunds) with Indian carriers and rupee amounts, as the guidelines allow instead of Olist.

generation.method: seeded Python generators (tables, tickets, PDFs) plus hand-written policies, extension tickets and eval cases
generation.note: No language model wrote any asset, so there is no provider or model to record; the seeded tables are byte-reproducible.

public_sources_referenced.name: Bitext retail/e-commerce chatbot dataset
public_sources_referenced.use: Intent taxonomy NAMES only (e.g. TRACK_DELIVERY, REFUND_REQUEST) for the ticket labels. No Bitext text or rows are included.

public_sources_referenced.name: Olist Brazilian e-commerce dataset
public_sources_referenced.use: NOT used. Replaced by the guide's allowed synthetic equivalent (Indian carriers, rupee amounts, abuse flags, refund approval tiers).

public_sources_referenced.name: Customer Support on Twitter
public_sources_referenced.use: NOT used. Recommended by the guide to calibrate how angry real customers sound; open follow-up (sentiment labels were not checked against real tweets).

public_sources_referenced.name: Amazon Reviews 2023 (McAuley Lab)
public_sources_referenced.use: NOT used. Product names in products.csv are invented.

foreign_key_check: enforced by tests/test_data.py (orders->customers, refunds/shipments/items->orders, ticket labels->visible order refs)
